one_liner: Senior Executive running DoD's sexual assault prevention and response office: setting department-wide prevention policy, leading senior staff, and dealing with Congress, OMB, GAO and the White House.
fit_summary: This Tier 2 SES job expects years of executive leadership plus expertise in prevention science or public health and enterprise program management. Daniel's public health response work (vaccination-site logistics, mpox meeting support) is relevant in spirit, but his resume shows no executive supervision, budget authority or prevention expertise. GS-9 to GS-12 public health, preparedness or program roles fit him now.
eligibility: Open to the public (the hiring paths include 'public'), so you do not need federal status, but you must show all five Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) and both Technical Qualifications (TQs) within your resume.

Technical Qualification 1 requires demonstrated expertise in behavioral science, public health, prevention science or a related field, including evidence-based primary prevention of sexual assault and other harmful behaviors.
Education cannot substitute for experience; the panel will judge you only on demonstrated executive and technical experience.
You must be able to obtain and keep a Secret security clearance.
Your resume must not exceed 2 pages; resumes over the limit are disqualified.
strategy: Be realistic and treat this posting mainly as a model for future applications. Apply only if you can honestly document executive-level leadership, supervision, and budget responsibility.

If you apply, write about your IEM work in terms of government-client outcomes: preparedness and readiness programs, policy support, and coordination with multiple agencies. Give your title, hours per week, scope, and dollar values exactly as they were.
Fit all five ECQs and both TQs into 2 pages by using one or two achievement bullets per ECQ. Include an enterprise-perspective line about national security or readiness.
Show his knowledge of the American system of government (ECQ 1), which his close following of politics and policy supports. His resume shows no work with Congress, so don't claim it.
Submit before 2026-11-10. Then apply in parallel to GS-level roles in preparedness, policy analysis, or legislative liaison, and to Virginia and Northern Virginia emergency-management jobs.
resume_bullets: Took part in public health seminars on response and recovery roles (2022–2024).
Facilitated full-scale and tabletop exercises for federal, state and private-sector clients (2022–2024).
interview_questions: Describe how you used data and program evaluation to change a policy or resource decision.
How would you gain the cooperation of the Military Services and other DoD Components on a prevention initiative they resist?
Tell us about a time you held staff accountable while leading them through organizational change.
How would you prepare for and handle a congressional inquiry or GAO review of the program?
watch_outs: The Technical Qualifications require subject-matter expertise in sexual assault prevention or prevention science that is not in your known background.
This is an SES role reviewed by an Executive Evaluation Panel; without senior executive experience you are unlikely to be rated highly qualified.
The 2-page limit is enforced by disqualification, so check the page count before you submit.
The job requires a Secret clearance and closes 2026-11-10.
